transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-18
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maria (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Laura (Miramar VP Eng), Ravi (Miramar Sec Arch), Sofia (Miramar DevOps), Aiden (PM)

Summary (auto):
POC scoping focused on private connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency requirements (US + EU), egress restrictions (no public internet for PHI), and benchmark success criteria for Miramar's clinical summarization workload. Agreed next steps: send private networking checklist, share AWS IDs, run benchmarks week of 7/27, follow up to review results and discuss Dedicated/Private options.

Topics: private networking, VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, region selection, KMS/HSM, SOC2 artifacts, benchmark targets (latency/throughput), timeline for POC

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maria: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving out time. I'm Maria from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Ethan our SE. Today we'd like to run through Miramar's networking constraints and what a quick POC would look like.
[00:15] Laura: Yeah thanks Maria, and hi Ethan. Quick context, we are building a clinical note summarization feature, must keep data in-region for patient privacy, and we need to understand if we can connect to Redwood without internet egress from our VPC.
[00:30] Ethan: Totally, understood. We'll cover VPC peering and PrivateLink options, plus the security artifacts we can provide. Can you confirm which regions you need?
[00:40] Ravi: Primary is us-east-1 for production, but a chunk of our customers are in EU (eu-west-1) and we need residency there as well. No PHI should leave those regions per our compliance.
[00:52] Maria: Got it. For the POC are you okay testing in us-east-1 first and then repeating in eu-west-1?
[00:58] Sofia: Yes, start us-east-1. We'll mirror the setup in EU if the POC passes. Also, important: our security team requires KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:12] Ethan: We can support KMS for envelope encryption of storage, and we emit audit logs — we'll share the schema. For networking we have two common paths: VPC peering (or inter-region peering) and AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints).
[01:27] Laura: Quick pros/cons?
[01:30] Ethan: Sure — VPC peering gives you a direct route between VPCs, simpler routing, lower latency potentially. But it requires route table updates and, depending on your org, might be harder cross-account or cross-region. PrivateLink gives you interface endpoints in your VPC and we present the service behind an endpoint — that avoids route table peering and is often preferred by security teams because you control endpoints and there's no transitive routing. However, PrivateLink can be slightly higher latency and there are per-endpoint ENIs and cost considerations.
[01:57] Ravi: We prefer no transit across public internet and more guarded control. PrivateLink sounds better from our policy perspective. Any caveats?
[02:05] Ethan: Biggest caveat is outbound egress policy: if your VPC has strict NAT rules, you'll need to allow traffic to the PrivateLink endpoint. Also if you want to stream responses, we need to ensure the endpoint supports the scale — we can provide the expected bandwidth per connection.
[02:20] Aiden: For benchmarking — what metrics should we be aiming for? Our product KPI is end-to-end latency under 500ms for 90% of calls on average commercial load, and throughput of about 50 requests per second during peak. Payloads are ~800-1200 tokens on average for summarization.
[02:38] Ethan: Helpful. For the POC typical targets we propose: p95 latency under 800ms for 1k token generation, and sustained throughput 50 RPS with concurrency 20. If you want tighter latency (like 300–400ms p95) we can recommend dedicated capacity and quantization profiles.
[02:56] Maria: Also want to call out cost trade-offs — dedicated vs hosted. For POC we can run on our hosted infra behind PrivateLink; if you need production SLA and predictable tail latencies, Dedicated or Private (customer-managed) might be better.
[03:11] Laura: Security items — SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS are must-haves. Does Redwood provide SOC2 reports and can we do a security review during POC?
[03:22] Maria: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II report and our security whitepaper. We can also do a security review — we usually run that parallel to the networking setup.
[03:30] Ravi: One more constraint — egress. We cannot allow PHI to egress to third-party regions or to the public internet. If you host in us-east-1 and we have clients in eu-west-1, how do you ensure data residency?
[03:45] Ethan: We can pin model serving to region-local clusters. For hosted API we have region selection and we can restrict the service to specific regions; for more strict requirements we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where you run the control plane in your environment or we deploy a private cluster in your VPC. For the POC, we'll run region-local instances: us-east-1 for your primary tests and eu-west-1 for the EU tests.
[04:05] Sofia: If we use PrivateLink, traffic stays in-region right?
[04:09] Ethan: Yes, PrivateLink endpoints point to an interface within the region. The main piece is to ensure the service endpoint you connect to is the region-local service. We'll share exact endpoint ARNs.
[04:18] Laura: Ok good. Benchmarks — what's the test plan?
[04:22] Ethan: We'll run a 3-step test plan: 1) Baseline single-request latency for representative payloads (512, 1k tokens). 2) Throughput test: ramp to target RPS (50) with sustained run 10 minutes to check tail latency and CPU/GPU utilization. 3) Failover/scaling: introduce bursts to validate autoscaling behavior and graceful degradation. We'll use your sample prompt set.
[04:42] Aiden: We'll provide a sample of 200 typical prompts and a 2-hour window for running the throughput test.
[04:48] Maria: Great. For metrics we'll capture p50/p90/p95, token/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, error rates, and network egress. We'll also deliver the raw logs and a simple spreadsheet with the numbers.
[04:59] Ravi: On encryption — we need keys in our KMS, not Redwood-managed keys. Is that supported?
[05:04] Ethan: Yes, customer-managed KMS keys for storage/envelope encryption is supported in Private and Dedicated deployments; for hosted we can also integrate with customer KMS in many cases — if not, we can do a bring-your-own-key workflow. We'll confirm specifics in the checklist.
[05:18] Laura: Timeline — how long to get PrivateLink or peering set up for POC?
[05:23] Maria: Typical is 1 week for networking setup if we have AWS account IDs and IAM contacts, then 1 week to run benchmarks and iterate, and a final week for results review and security signoff — so ~3 weeks. If any legal or procurement holds, that can extend it.
[05:38] Sofia: We can get AWS IDs this week. We'll need a runbook of steps so our infra team can do changes during a maintenance window.
[05:45] Maria: We'll send a Private networking checklist with the exact steps (VPC CIDR, account IDs, security group ports, endpoint names) and an estimated change window.
[05:54] Ethan: One operational note on DNS — with PrivateLink you'll need to create an interface endpoint and optionally enable private DNS for the endpoint so the SDK resolves to the endpoint automatically. If you prefer explicit endpoints we can provide hostnames. Also ensure your egress firewall allows the service port.
[06:12] Ravi: Do you support mutual TLS or client certs on top of PrivateLink?
[06:16] Ethan: The control plane uses mTLS internally — for POC we typically use IAM and TLS. If you need mutual TLS at the network layer we can explore that in Private / Dedicated options. I'll flag that as a security follow-up.
[06:28] Laura: Any limits on concurrent streams? Our UI streams partial summaries as they arrive, so streaming support is important.
[06:35] Ethan: We support streaming. For the POC we'll instrument streaming connections and measure sustained open connections. We typically provision for hundreds of concurrent streaming clients per pod but we'll validate.
[06:47] Maria: Ok, quick recap so we capture success criteria: 1) POC runs in us-east-1 using PrivateLink, 2) p95 latency under 800ms for 1k-token workloads, 3) sustain 50 RPS with acceptable error rate (<0.1%), 4) no PHI egress outside pinned regions, 5) SOC2 and KMS integration validated. Anything to add?
[07:08] Aiden: Add streaming behaviour must not exceed 1.5x latency compared to non-streaming API.
[07:12] Ravi: And audit logs forwarded to our SIEM within 5 minutes.
[07:16] Maria: We'll add those items.
[07:19] Laura: Regarding cost — for the POC will there be charges for PrivateLink or test infra?
[07:24] Maria: We'll cover the baseline test infra; PrivateLink data-transfer and endpoint costs follow AWS pricing and are typically borne by the customer, but we'll give an estimate. For longer pilots we can discuss discounted reserved capacity.
[07:37] Sofia: One more point — network egress from our subnets is blocked by default. We'll open a temporary maintenance window to create the endpoint and adjust route tables. We'll provide a contact for infra changes.
[07:48] Maria: Perfect. We'll include exact IAM permissions and the change window in the checklist. Also sending SOC2 artifacts and the redwood-private-networking-checklist.docx link in the follow-up.
[07:59] Ethan: On benchmark config I plan to run two model variants — a 7B quantized profile and a 13B float profile — to show latency/cost tradeoffs. We'll capture token cost per request so you can evaluate unit economics.
[08:14] Aiden: That would be useful. For our internal cost model we need per-request token cost and expected token/sec for typical sessions.
[08:21] Ethan: We'll include a spreadsheet with cost per 1k tokens for each profile and the measured throughput numbers.
[08:27] Laura: Any regulatory paperwork needed for EU residency?
[08:31] Maria: We have Data Processing Addendum templates and can sign region-specific residency clauses. We'll include that in the follow-up package.
[08:39] Ravi: Ok. If the POC looks good, what's the path to production? Dedicated nodes? Private on-prem?
[08:46] Maria: Multiple options: 1) Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in the region under your account with SLA and capacity guarantees; 2) Redwood Private: deploy a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC or our validated on-prem package; either will give you stronger isolation. We'll outline the tradeoffs post-POC.
[09:02] Aiden: Any support for FIPS/HSM for keys?
[09:06] Ethan: Yes, we integrate with customer HSM/KMS approaches for Private deployments; for hosted we have options but depending on region we may need dedicated arrangements. We'll note that.
[09:16] Laura: Sounds good. Last question — can we do a smoke-run next Wednesday at 10am?
[09:21] Sofia: That should work if we get the checklist today.
[09:24] Maria: We'll send the checklist and SOC2 by tomorrow EOD, and we'll aim to schedule the smoke-run for 2026-07-22 10:00am ET — if that works we'll lock it after you confirm account IDs.
[09:37] (short crosstalk)
[09:45] Maria: Great, I'll capture action items and send notes. Thanks everyone.

--- End transcript ---
